# Ugarte's Red Dream: A New Chapter at Old Trafford

The buzz around Manchester United's training ground was electric as Manuel Ugarte stepped off the plane at Manchester Airport, clutching a small bag and wearing a quiet, determined smile. After weeks of negotiations between the two clubs, the deal was finally done — €50 million, with the promise of more to come if things went well.

Ugarte had grown up watching his heroes play in the biggest stadiums in the world. As a young boy in Uruguay, he had dreamed of one day pulling on a famous shirt and running out in front of tens of thousands of passionate supporters. Now, at just 23 years old, that dream was becoming a reality.

Erik ten Hag had made no secret of his desire to strengthen the heart of his midfield. Casemiro had been a warrior for United, but the demands of modern football required depth, energy, and relentless pressing — qualities that Ugarte had displayed consistently during his time at Paris Saint-Germain.

As Ugarte signed his five-year contract, he paused and looked around the room at the assembled staff and officials. "I came here to win," he said simply, his voice steady and sincere. "I will give everything I have."

Dan Ashworth nodded approvingly. The sporting director knew they had secured something special — a player hungry, driven, and ready to help rebuild United's proud legacy one hard tackle at a time.

Any other questions?
